summary: For c1, the old harness could scan a balanced depth-1001 flow collection before the change. After the change, the scanner rejects it at the default limit of 1000; reaching the same behavior requires a higher configured limit that the old harness never sets.

claims.necessity_reason: The supported capability is scanning a balanced flow collection at depth 1001. Before the change the scanner permits that depth without special setup; afterward its new guard requires a limit above 1000, which the fixed target cannot set.

before.requirement: Reach scanning of a balanced depth-1001 flow collection. The scanner does not consult the configurable maximum when increasing flow depth.
before.reason: The old increase function rejects only INT_MAX. The fixed harness forwards the finite input and continues scanning, so its default setup is an equivalent route to this scanning capability.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: Opening flow indicators enter the collection-start route.
The route invokes the old increase function and emits a start token on success.

after.requirement: Reach scanning of the same balanced depth-1001 flow collection under a supported limit above 1000, such as 2000.
after.reason: The new guard rejects the 1001st opening bracket at the default limit of 1000. The old harness has no setter call, so input bytes cannot reach the supported higher-limit setup.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: Defines the setter that can raise the limit.
Declares the supported configurable nesting limit.

claims.comparison_reason: The tuple remains scanner scan, balanced depth-1001 flow input, the capability to scan it, and its reachability. Before, the old scanner has no nesting-limit guard; after, the new guard makes the target's fixed default setup block that capability.
